left_out: Officiant on Demand, Chicago (officiantondemand.com/elopement): all-inclusive elopement packages but every price is printed as a range with no 'from' or 'starting at' (Chicago Lakeshore & Skyline Package 'Price: $1900 - $2100', up to 15 guests; Chicago Gardens 'Price: $2199 - $5399', limit 20 guests; The Lyttle House 'Price: $4500 - $5500', limit 20 guests). The brief allows the low end as amount only when the page states a starting price, so none is listed.

Dare to Dream (daretodream.nyc/weddings/): twelve priced items (e.g. Central Park, Vows Renewal Package) but the page text does not make clear which price belongs to which name (the prices sit in a filter widget), so no package is quoted.
Verandas Events, Houston Heights (verandasevents.com): the page prints 'Quick "I do" $399 Elopements' with no inclusions and no guest count for it, so it is not listed as a package.

Houston: only two providers (The Little Glass Chapel, The Middleton Venue) printed an elopement price in curl-readable HTML that I could reach. The Reserve on Cypress Creek ($4,500 Mon-Thu, up to 70 guests), The Juliana ($6,000 full day) and the Barn at Lacey Farms ($2399-$2899, Burton TX, not Houston) are full-day venue rentals or outside Houston, not elopement packages.
Pop The Knot has no Houston page (its city list has Dallas, Chicago, LA, NYC and others, not Houston; /houston-elopement-packages/ returns 404).
Simply Eloped Chicago (simplyeloped.com): every Chicago venue card says 'Check Pricing' with no price printed on the page.
Little Church of the West, Las Vegas: the packages page has no package price in its curl HTML text.
The Penrose House (near Dallas, 45 min away): all-inclusive micro wedding 'from $10,000', not an elopement-size price and not in Dallas, so not listed.
notes: Web search was unavailable for this run (the per-turn search budget was used up by the other researchers), so I did not discover providers with a search engine. I started from provider pages that the city researchers had already cached under .cache/raw/<city>/ (used only as leads), re-downloaded every cited page myself with curl into .cache/raw/packages/, and probed a few well-known Las Vegas chapel domains directly. The list is therefore not a survey of the whole market; Houston is the thinnest city (two providers). Place labels are literal: Hurst is in the Dallas-Fort Worth area (not Dallas), Katy and Missouri City/Stafford are Houston-area suburbs, Bronx is New York City. Time-limited prices: Albertson Wedding Chapel says its package prices expire 10/31/2026; Vegas Weddings was running a sale ending October 31; Lucky Wedding Day showed an 'October SPECIAL - $50 OFF' banner; Perfect Wedding NYC shows a sale price beside the original price. The Middleton Venue page footer reads 2023, so its price may be older than the others. Pop The Knot prints the same $3,499 on its Dallas (https://www.poptheknot.com/dallas-elopement-packages/) and New York (https://www.poptheknot.com/new-york-elopement-packages/) pages; only Chicago and Los Angeles are listed here to avoid repeating one product four times. Other priced packages seen on the same cited pages but not listed because of the 16-package cap: Drive Up & Wed Kiss & Go $250 and The Heartfelt $975 (Hurst); NYC Wedding Factory Gold Package $1000 (ceremony + photography session); Perfect Wedding NYC All-Inclusive Ceremony Package $3,770; Albertson Legacy $1890; Lucky Wedding Day Sweet Package $449.99; Astoria Banquets Elopement Ceremony $1,200 (Buffalo Grove, Chicago suburb); Little Vegas Chapel Love & Cherish $299; Elope to Chicago Elopement Package $1110 (2 hours, up to 12 guests) and Tiny Wedding Package $2000 (4 hours, up to 20 guests). luckyweddingday.com is slow (about 13 s with curl) and timed out once in verify_quotes.py's urllib fetch; its text is now cached in .cache/pages/, so re-runs are fast, but if that cache is cleared a re-run may need a retry. guests is null where the page states no guest count for that package. The Little Glass Chapel page lists three packages in a block where it is not clear which feature lines belong to Quick "I Do", so only the 30-minute access line next to its price is used.
